Verified: Petrov et al., RecSys 2026, “Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Really Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?” PCTM counts directed, forward transitions across training histories: C_ba = Σ_{d=1}^W γ_d N_ba^(d), where N_ba^(d) counts a occurring d positions after b and γ₁=1. Uniform Dirichlet smoothing gives P̂(a|b) = (C_ba + τ/|I|)/(Σ_i C_bi + τ). Ranking uses s(a|h) = Σ_j w_j log P̂(a|h_j) + λ log p_pop(a), with h_j indexed newest-first and p_pop(a) = (f_a+1)/(Σ_i f_i+|I|). This is weighted log pooling—a product of transition experts—not an arithmetic average of probabilities. [Paper and equations](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.19833v1).

Recency acts twice: distance decay during transition counting, then normalized history weights during inference. History kernels include exponential decay and a head–tail mixture reserving mass ρ for the newest k interactions. Selected Amazon settings use windows 10–20 and history cap 50; popularity coefficients are −0.04 for Beauty and zero for Sports/Toys. Thus explicit transition counting, smoothing and recency aggregation define the reference; popularity correction is optional, not universally necessary. Individual contributions remain unproven without ablations. [Supplementary definitions/configurations](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.19833v1#A1).

Evaluation uses matched eSASRec splits, full-catalogue ranking, seen-item filtering and NDCG@10; hyperparameters are selected on an inner training holdout before refitting. At least one pairwise probe beats both Transformer reproductions on Beauty, Sports, Toys and MovieLens-1M, but trails on MovieLens-20M. These results do not establish gains on the requested four Amazon categories or sampled-candidate HR@10 protocol; that transfer requires matched validation. [Official evaluation protocol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spotify-research/sequential-capacity-probes/main/docs/PROTOCOL.md).
